rationale: Three lenses ran on the frontend half (blind, edge-case with repo access, acceptance against spec). The edge-case lens verified the critical finding empirically by mounting the chat block against a real valtio store rather than by reading code: every previously green test mocked useSnapshot globally in the unit project, so the whole surface feature was dead in production while 700+ tests passed. That is the same failure shape as backend CR-001 — a test harness that removed the very thing under test. All 14 findings were fixed in this round (two parallel fix agents with disjoint file ownership) and are recorded here as resolved-during-review; the fixes are re-checked in code-review-check.json. Two orchestrator decisions overrode a fix agent: crossOrigin="anonymous" on media elements was reverted (it forces a CORS-mode fetch and breaks every host that does not send Access-Control-Allow-Origin, while adding nothing once the consent gate exists and cross-site cookies are already withheld by the SameSite default), and the silent refusal of an invalid surface was given user-visible feedback (no catalog component renders a failed check inline, so refusing silently read as a dead button). Deferred (recorded, not blocking): multi-surface handling has unit coverage only because the backend emits one surface per turn; checks scoped inside a List are deliberately not enforced client-side (relative paths are unevaluatable at the surface root) and rely on server-side intake validation; A2UI cannot distinguish a submit button from a decline button, so the client validity gate blocks every action on an invalid surface.

findings.problem: structuredClone was called on values read out of a valtio store. valtio snapshots are proxy-compare tracking Proxies (not frozen plain objects in 2.1.5), and structuredClone refuses to clone a Proxy — every surface threw DataCloneError.
findings.impact: Verified by mounting the chat block against a real valtio proxy: the exception was swallowed by the surrounding try/catch and every A2UI surface rendered the 'could not be displayed' fallback. The feature was dead in production while the unit suite stayed green, because setupTests.unit.ts mocks useSnapshot globally.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a JSON round-trip that reads through the proxy get-traps, and add a test in the integration project that uses a real valtio store.

findings.problem: The prefill data model was shallow-spread, leaving nested objects and arrays as valtio proxies.
findings.impact: A re-answered surface replayed proxy-backed values into the SDK data model; array-valued answers (multi-select) were the concrete case.
findings.recommendation: Serialize the prefill map once and parse it back in a memo keyed on the serialized string.

findings.problem: A surface whose 'root' component never resolved (stream cut short by Stop, or an agent that named its root differently) fell through to the SDK's gray '[Loading root...]' placeholder.
findings.impact: A stopped generation left an inert grey box in the chat with no explanation and no recovery.
findings.recommendation: Report missingRoot from the processed components model and degrade to the fallback, except while the message is still streaming; reset the error boundary when the envelope set changes.

findings.problem: Only the first createSurface envelope in a message was tracked, so a second surface rendered but could never be answered or marked read-only.
findings.impact: The wire format permits several surfaces per message; the answer bookkeeping silently applied to the first one only.
findings.recommendation: Track all created surface ids and resolve prefill, read-only state and replaceHistoryIndex per surface.

findings.problem: The action handler was synchronous and dropped the submit promise: a double click created two turns, and a rejection escaped as an unhandled rejection.
findings.impact: Duplicate answers to one question, and a failed submit left the form locked with no error shown.
findings.recommendation: Latch synchronously before the first await, await the promise, and report pre-chip failures through the existing stream-error path.

findings.problem: Nothing aggregated a surface's checks: the SDK injects isValid only into the props of the component that declares them, and agents attach checks to the inputs, not to the button.
findings.impact: An invalid form submitted anyway, and the server-side answer validation rejected it with a 422 the user could not act on.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate every absolute-path check against the surface root before submitting, and tell the user why the submit was refused.
findings.status: RESOLVED during review (orchestrator added the user-visible toast; a silent refusal reads as a dead button)

findings.problem: A sanitized https media URL was mounted immediately. The URL is authored by the agent, which is steerable via prompt injection, and the app has no CSP and no trusted-domain registry (verified: no Content-Security-Policy, img-src or allowlist anywhere in src, index.html or vite.config.ts).
findings.impact: Zero-click exfiltration: rendering a surface makes the browser request an attacker-chosen host from the user's IP, with conversation data encoded in the URL query.
findings.recommendation: Defer the request behind a consent gate that names the target host, and strip the referrer. A full fix (server-side media proxy or a domain allowlist) is a product decision and is not attempted here.
findings.status: RESOLVED during review (residual risk recorded: a user who clicks still discloses their IP to the named host)

findings.problem: DateTimeInput rendered nothing when the agent set neither enableDate nor enableTime.
findings.impact: A required date field the user cannot see or fill, blocking the whole surface.
findings.recommendation: Default to the date picker; a placeholder still could not satisfy a required check.

findings.problem: ChoicePicker options with a missing, empty or duplicate value rendered as selectable controls.
findings.impact: The control could only ever submit [''], which the server then rejects as not offered by the surface.
findings.recommendation: Normalize options, drop unusable ones, and degrade to a text note when none survive.

findings.problem: A bound value naming options the surface does not declare, or naming one option twice, was passed straight through; single-selection mode let the DOM arbitrate between two checked radios.
findings.impact: Inconsistent client state and an answer the server rejects. Numeric caps for multipleSelection are not derivable client-side (the condition is an arbitrary expression tree) and remain enforced by the checks mechanism plus server-side intake.
findings.recommendation: Filter the bound value to declared options, de-duplicate, and resolve a single selection in single mode.

findings.problem: Only 25 of the 59 Icon enum names the backend advertises to the model had a mapping; the rest rendered an empty box.
findings.impact: The prompt offers the model names that render as nothing.
findings.recommendation: Map every name that has a design-system counterpart, resolve the remainder to a real fallback glyph, and derive the enum from the catalog schema in the test so the mapping cannot drift.

findings.problem: The number variant of TextField wrote its value as a string, and Slider never wrote its effective value when the data model had none.
findings.impact: Numeric checks compared against a string and failed; a slider left untouched submitted no value at all.
findings.recommendation: Parse the number variant into a real number (undefined for an empty or unparsable buffer) and have Slider write its effective value on mount when the model has none.

findings.problem: The assistant form read only the new interactive_enabled boolean.
findings.impact: Between deploy and the data migration, an assistant saved under the legacy interactive_features object displayed as disabled and would have been saved back as disabled.
findings.recommendation: Prefer the explicit boolean, fall back to any enabled flag in the legacy object, and mark the fallback as temporary rollout compatibility.

findings.problem: The assistant form imported the component list from the registry module, pulling the entire A2UI renderer and its dependencies into the assistants bundle.
findings.impact: Unnecessary bundle weight on a page that only needs the list of names.
findings.recommendation: Import from the dependency-free components module.
